children: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta Platforms to pay $25 billion to the state after a jury found the social -media company misled users about its data-privacy practices.
The decision came down hours before Meta is scheduled to report its third-quarter financial results.

The jury found Meta liable last month for violating New Mexico's unfair practices law. It determined the company deceived users about data privacy, its efforts to fight hate speech and misinformation, and its handling of a third-party app tied to the 2018 Cambridge Analytica data breach, where a consulting firm harvested tens of millions of Facebook users' data without their consent.

"The harm in this matter is difficult to overstate, and goes to the heart of Facebook's basic business proposition," said Judge Francis Mathew in his order. "To induce users to provide their personal information to Facebook, Facebook made many false promises respecting the security and control of that data over the course of more than a decade."
